chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام:
Concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic,
"and He gives life to the earth after its death."

He عليه السلام said: "He does not give it life by rainfall; rather, Allah sends men who bring life through justice, so the earth comes to life by the revival of justice. And the establishment of one hadd therein is more beneficial on the earth than forty mornings of rainfall."

key_terms.الْأَرْضَ: the earth; here, society and the land brought to flourishing
key_terms.الْعَدْلِ: justice; the equitable order by which society is revived
key_terms.مَوْتِهَا: its death; its lifeless or ruined condition

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the Quranic phrase "He gives life to the earth after its death"?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse as referring not merely to physical revival through rain, but to the moral and social revival brought about by justice. It emphasizes that the implementation of divine justice gives true life to the earth and benefits society more deeply than abundant rainfall.
